description: The egui stack moves as one version or not at all. ecolor and emath were missing from this list and renovate opened PR #22 for ecolor alone: it resolved, and produced TWO ecolor (0.35.0 and 0.36.1) and TWO emath, because epaint 0.35 holds the older pair. A lone bump here is never mergeable.
egui-wgpu is what ties wgpu in -- 0.35 wants wgpu ^29, 0.36 wants ^30 -- so an egui bump and a wgpu bump are one upgrade, and separating them produces two PRs that each cannot resolve.

The wasm-bindgen family releases in lockstep and every pin here is exact, so each crate's requirement is unsatisfiable until its siblings move with it. Measured: PRs #3 #4 #5 #6 #7 each FAILED to resolve alone (`failed to select a version for js-sys`, and so on round the ring); the same five pins applied together resolve cleanly. Renovate reported this as `renovate/artifacts: Artifact file update failure`, which reads as a bot problem and is really this.

wasm-bindgen-test is in the group rather than beside it because squallar-web/Cargo.toml notes that the resolver picks the train satisfying the wasm-bindgen pin, and the workflow's `cargo tree -i wasm-bindgen` gate is what holds that single-versioned.

dark-light is held below 3 by user ruling, 2026-08-31. The API we call is unchanged across the major -- `detect() -> Result<Mode, Error>` with the same three variants -- so this is not a porting cost, it is a behaviour change that reads as a version bump.

2.0.0's freedesktop arm wraps the portal read in `future::timeout(Duration::from_millis(25), ...)`. 3.0.0 removes the timeout entirely: `detect()` is a bare `zbus::blocking` call on the D-Bus session with no deadline. That trades a known failure (the 25 ms deadline expiring under load and answering Light, which squallar/src/platform.rs compensates for with retries) for an unbounded block, and unbounded blocking is what `offload large ops` exists to forbid.
3.0.0 also adds subscribe()/Watcher/stream(), which is a better answer to runtime theme changes than polling detect(). Taking the major should be that piece of work, deliberately, not a merge button.

Crates vendored under vendor/ and substituted into the graph by [patch.crates-io] in the root Cargo.toml. This rule comes after the egui group on purpose: packageRules merge in order, so the disable here is what wins for walkers.

ignorePaths does not cover these. The version requirement that renovate edits lives in the ROOT Cargo.toml's [workspace.dependencies] (and, for geo-types, in a member manifest) -- not under vendor/ -- so the file it rewrites was never ignored.

Raising one of these pins does not fail. cargo stops applying the patch, silently, and resolves the registry copy instead: measured on PR #21, `cargo metadata` exits 0 with no warning and squallar-egui resolves pmtiles 0.24.0 from crates.io while the vendored 0.23.0 sits in the workspace, still compiling, reachable from nothing. The build stays green and the fix the vendoring exists to carry is simply gone.

walkers 0.58.0 was measured to do the same once geo-types moves to 0.7.20 (PR #20) -- and it re-adds 78 crates to the graph. Today it errors only because the stale geo-types pin happens to block it; that brake is an accident and PR #20 removes it.
bzip2-rs is listed defensively. It is reachable only as a path dependency of vendor/nexrad-data, so no manifest states a version renovate could edit today.

Bumping any of these is hand work: port the upstream release into vendor/, keep package.version exactly equal to the pin (a patch is only accepted for a version that satisfies the requirement), and update that crate's VENDORED.md.
